skill.displayName: AI Short Film Finalization — Route C (Flow Free)

llm.summary: The skill is not clearly malicious, but it asks an agent to control a logged-in Google browser session and write local media outputs in ways broader than its finalization description.

dimensions.detail: The frontmatter describes post-generation finalization, while the body expands to a full RPA generation pipeline using Google Vids, Flow, Gemini, Playwright, CDP, and existing Google login state. The director review console is disclosed, but the authenticated browser automation is broader than the initial description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs launching or connecting to Chrome on a DevTools port, reusing the user's logged-in Google session, using human-like automation helpers, and downloading generated videos through the browser request context. These are high-impact actions without clear domain, tab, consent, or per-action containment.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No automatic installer or hidden persistence was found, but the instructions tell the user or agent to install playwright-core into a hardcoded managed Node workspace and rely on hardcoded local runtime paths.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: FFmpeg media extraction and review-package file writes are proportionate to film review, but authenticated browser automation and anti-bot-style interaction patterns are broader and riskier than a simple local finalization tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: I found no background service, privilege escalation, credential theft, or durable persistence. The main privilege concern is use of an already-authenticated browser session and repeated overwriting of generated review outputs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a skill that may drive your logged-in Google browser session and perform local media generation/editing. Review and constrain any CDP/Playwright use, avoid running it against unrelated browser tabs or accounts, and sanitize storyboard titles before running the review generator.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell, filesystem, ffmpeg, and browser automation are consistent with the full workflow described in the body, but the skill does not clearly scope or declare those capabilities up front.
[TP4] expected: The review package generator is explicitly documented in the body, so I do not treat this as deceptive tooling. The concern is narrower: the frontmatter and included artifacts do not cleanly match the broad pipeline described later.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: the body openly documents RPA generation, but that scope conflicts with the frontmatter's post-generation finalization framing.
[SDI-2] expected: Confirmed: the artifact instructs CDP connection to a logged-in Chrome session for Google services. That is useful for the stated RPA workflow but high-impact and insufficiently contained.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed: the stated use case says shots are already generated, while later instructions include generating and regenerating shots through external Google tools.
[OH1] expected: Confirmed that storyboard titles are used directly in clip, audio, and frame filenames. This is expected output generation, but titles should be sanitized to avoid malformed paths, accidental overwrites, or path-handling edge cases.
[staticScan] expected: The static scan was clean, which lowers confidence of outright malware but does not remove the artifact-backed scoping concerns.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal reported no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this was treated as supportive telemetry, not decisive.
